text:
marta: Heads-up: HydrA reporting a sustained spike and 429s on their dedicated pool since 10:05 UTC. Baseline QPS ~240, sudden sustained peak ~1.2k for ~6 mins. Customer says autoscale didn't add extra workers and they're seeing 20-50ms extra queue latency then 429. Request ids: rID=hydra-ef34, hydra-ef35
alex: :eyes: pulling metrics now. which pool? hydra-prod-gpu-pool
ben: saw an alert earlier: pool utilization hit 96% for 4m; autoscaler triggered but scaled from 3->4 and stalled. cooldown is 3m. logs show tailback on the enqueue path.
lisa: can you paste the autoscale policy? also any noisy-tenant throttles? sometimes a single tenant can saturate the batcher.
marta: autoscale policy: min=3 max=10 target_cpu=65 target_util=0.7 scale_up_step=1 cooldown_up=3m
alex: infra metrics: batch queue depth spiked to 520 requests, avg token latency 110ms, worker gpu_util 98% on node-2. Also saw frequent small tensor allocations from tenant=hydra-experiments which correlate with high copy overhead.
ben: stack logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T10:07:12Z enqueuer: queue_len=512 pool=hydra-prod-gpu-pool
2026-03-17T10:07:14Z autoscaler: scale_up requested -> adding 1 worker
2026-03-17T10:09:30Z autoscaler: worker join delay >90s, scaling observed as stalled
2026-03-17T10:10:00Z serving: 429 returned due to request_timeout
```
marta: customer notes they run large in-context windows and a few jobs have long seq len ~6k tokens during spikes.
lisa: OK - hypothesis: autoscaler is conservative, and high per-request sequence lengths plus a noisy tenant tying up GPU memory causes slow worker init. We should: 1) temporarily increase headroom (min=4) or bump max=12 + enable burst capacity; 2) patch autoscaler to allow scale_up_step=2 for this pool; 3) mark noisy tenant for isolation (move to separate pool or rate limit).
alex: I can manually add 2 workers now to relieve pressure. Doing it. :shipit:
ops-bot: manual_scale: pool=hydra-prod-gpu-pool action=add nodes=2 by=alex
ben: after manual add queue depth dropping to 80, 429s stopped. but we need long-term fix.
marta: action items: - propose resizing baseline to 5 workers (from 3) for hydra-prod-gpu-pool - set target_util lower to 60% for production pools with heavy long-context workloads - open tenant isolation request for hydra-experiments - create warmup job for new workers to reduce join delay
lisa: also suggest probing kernel logs for memory OOMs or cuda init slowdowns; attach repro steps and a short eval harness that mimics their seq len distribution.
ben: I'll file a ticket and schedule a quick call with HydrA SRE to confirm SLA expectations. thanks team :thumbsup:
marta: thanks — I'll update the customer and keep this thread for postmortem notes.
